Middleware beats prompt-only policy for tool risk.
Record distributions, versions and gate outcomes for every decision.

body.text: Why this matters

Harnesses are where agents become software. The planner can be clever and still be unsafe, slow or bankrupt if every micro-decision is another frontier completion. LangChain’s public Jev post shows two concrete seams — model routing middleware and Auto Mode tool gating. TenthMatrix generalises those seams into a full loop you can implement with Jev or with any calibrated decision backend.

body.label: Independence
body.text: This is TenthMatrix sample logic. It is not a copy of LangChain AutoModeMiddleware source, and it is not an official TypeSafe cookbook.
Observability

Emit OpenTelemetry spans for each decision with attributes: model_version, question_ids, latency_ms, network_ms, argmax, confidence, gate_result, benchmark_suite_version. Without that, you cannot debug silent policy drift when jev-latest moves.
Limitations
A harness cannot invent ground truth. If your safety labels are wrong, a fast model will reliably enforce the wrong policy. Start with synthetic + shadowed production traces before enforcing denies.
Extended implementation notes

Conclusion
The harness is the product. Jev is one possible engine for the decision seams. The architecture remains valuable even if you swap engines.

faqs.q: How do I implement this in Rust?
faqs.a: Model the gate as a pure function over DecisionResponse → Enum, call the HTTP System One API with reqwest, and keep criteria in versioned config. Unofficial crates like jev-sdk exist; prefer official SDKs when available for your stack.
See /insights/benchmarks/v1/ and the Benchmark Lab page for suite definitions and JSONL schemas.
